answer: A market buying pigment assays of shale can require a separate bond for every report. Commit the result before a public randomness beacon selects samples for independent lab retesting. Proven fabrication forfeits the bond, which stays locked through the audit window. Choose audit probability p and bond B so p times B exceeds the maximum fraudulent payout. There is no signup reward, and one bond cannot back simultaneous reports. More aliases therefore require more locked capital while each false claim has negative expected profit. This assumes reliable retesting.
